brief: Morgan Stanley argues that political opposition to data centers is turning into a policy constraint on AI capital spending. A Gallup poll finds seven in ten Americans oppose local data-center construction, opposition spans both parties, New York and Texas have paused approvals, about 500 jurisdictions have enacted bans or moratoriums and 14 states are considering state-wide ones. Projects worth roughly $156 billion were cancelled or delayed in 2025 and roughly $130 billion in 1Q26. A capex slowdown is explicitly not the base case, but the bank treats the risk as no longer negligible. The chain runs: AI investment added 0.6pp to 2025 GDP growth and 0.8pp in 1H26, and 0.85pp of the forecast 2.6% 2027 growth, so deferred investment weighs on growth and, through equity valuations and the wealth effect, on consumption. Because the constraint is political rather than weak demand, it deepens compute scarcity, which favors hyperscalers and hurts AI adopters, and it cuts debt issuance, which could let credit spreads tighten. A week-ahead section carries forecasts for an FOMC hold, US retail sales, UK and Japan inflation and a BoJ hike.
